caveats: Anchor sets are not random samples of any population. They are the relevant works that an independent route reached, or an outside list.
An overlap is a probe of the v3.1 search on those works. It is not an estimate of how many relevant works the query finds.
A miss can reflect scope (for example tier-2 chemical terms, which v3.1 does not search) or OpenAlex matching. The title-level reason is only a hint.
Each probe asks OpenAlex only about the anchors listed in that call. It does not scan the corpus.
Sets are reported separately and never pooled.

sets.route: ORCID DOI ingest (source_run_id family orcid-doi-ingest) and ROR researcher DOI ingest (ror-researcher-doi-ingest); published and plastic_related true in the index
sets.independence: Route: independent of the search. These works were fetched by DOI only, with the v3.1 search switched off (scripts/ingest_orcid_dois.py, with_query=False). Selection: not independent of the vocabulary. Before merge each record had to pass a local rule built from the v3.1 core, qualified and exclusion terms plus tier-2 chemical terms (passes_query), so every anchor matches those terms. Of the 144 anchors, 49 are judged plastic-related by the assisted model, 1 by owner review, 78 are kept by the chemical-term rule after the model said not plastic-related, and 16 rest on the rule alone.
sets.verdict: route independent of the search, but selection used the same term list: a consistency check, not independent coverage

sets.route: Europe PMC audit (europepmc-audit): DOI list resolved in OpenAlex

The DOI lookups applied the v3.1 search: build_doi_url defaults to with_query=True (src/atlas/ingest/europepmc_audit.py), so only works that matched the query were merged. The Europe PMC benchmark is an outside list, but this route did not reach the Atlas independently, so it is not probed here.

Not independent and not probed: the overview is the Atlas's own published output, built from the corpus that the query populates, so it cannot test the query against an outside source.
